To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
microtubules are nucleated by the centrosomes in a process requiring both γ-tubulin and the centrioles.
the MTOCs of animal cells contain at least three different types of protein complexes, which are involved in microtubule nucleation, microtubule anchoring, and microtubule organization.
the functional components of microturbule-organizing centres (MTOCs) are the proteins that regulate microtubule assembly and the nucleation of microtubular arrays.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the organization of microtubular structures.
the functional properties of the microtubes and the MTOCs, and with the mechanisms by which MTOCs control microtubule assembly.
the functional components of microtuble-organizing centers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MTOCs are not only sites for microtubule nucleation but also sites of control over microtubule dynamics.
the MTOCs are the most important and complex cellular organelles, which play a key role in many cellular functions.
MTOCs serve as a platform for microtubule nucleation, as a template for microtubules to assemble and organize, and as an anchoring site for microtubular ends.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MTOC proteins are the functional components of the microtubes and are the main factors for the assembly of the microtubbles.
MTOCs are not simply sites where microtubules are nucleated but rather that they also affect the organization and structure of microtubular arrays.
MTOCs are the sites at which microtubule assembly is initiated, and they are responsible for the organization of the microtuble arrays in the cytoplasm and the spindle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the centrosome is a multifunctional organelle, which plays a key role in the regulation of cell division.
microtubule nucleation and anchoring are two distinct processes that can be regulated independently.
microtubules have a remarkable ability to nucleate from multiple sites within a cell and that this property is regulated in a spatial and temporal manner by MTOCs.
